verdict.rationale: SES supports inbound mail: MX-pointed receipt rules can store raw MIME messages in S3, publish to SNS, or trigger a Lambda function, and a community user confirms building exactly this pattern (Lambda dissects the email and forwards it to an HTTP endpoint). However, SES itself only delivers raw MIME to S3/SNS/Lambda — there's no native webhook delivery or automatic header/attachment parsing API, so developers must write their own Lambda-based parser/forwarder to get 'parsed messages to your webhook.' Missing for 10: a first-party parsed-message webhook/API delivery mechanism (vs. raw MIME + custom Lambda), and independent hands-on validation of attachment parsing reliability.
